ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the primary coil of an ideal transformer is connected to an AC power source, and all meters in the figure are ideal meters. When the sliding contact P of the slide rheostat slides upward, how does the reading of voltmeter V change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: When the sliding contact P of the slide rheostat slides upward, the reading of voltmeter V becomes larger
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the figure is the primary coil of the ideal transformer; the primary coil is connected to an AC power source, and an ammeter is also connected in series in the circuit. On the right side is the secondary-coil circuit: the upper end of the secondary coil first passes through a series resistor R1 and then is connected to the upper bus; the lower end of the secondary coil is connected to the lower bus. Voltmeter V is connected across the upper and lower buses behind R1, so it measures the voltage across the parallel load. The load part on the right has several parallel branches, among which the rightmost one is the slide rheostat; the slider P is connected to the upper bus, and the lower end of the slide rheostat is connected to the lower bus. Then reason: when slider P slides upward, the length of resistance wire connected into the circuit from slider P to the lower end of the slide rheostat becomes longer, so the resistance connected into this branch becomes larger. The primary coil of the ideal transformer is connected to a fixed AC power source, so the equivalent voltage provided by the secondary coil is unchanged; ideal meters do not affect the circuit. The branches behind R1 can be regarded as a parallel load. The resistance of the slide-rheostat branch becomes larger, making the total resistance of the parallel load become larger. Thus the total current in the secondary-coil circuit decreases, and the voltage drop across series resistor R1 decreases. When the total voltage of the secondary coil is unchanged, the voltage drop across R1 decreases, so the voltage across the parallel load at the rear end of R1 increases. Voltmeter V is exactly measuring this voltage, so the reading of V becomes larger.
